name: Minecraft: Gate
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Gate, a fast and lightweight Minecraft Java proxy written in Go that links your servers into one network, with a Lite mode that routes players by hostname. Installs any release, checked against GitHub's checksums.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Minecraft: Gate. Downloads a Gate release for the node's CPU from GitHub
# and checks it against GitHub's checksum. config.yml is never touched once
# it exists, and the program is only replaced once the new one checks out.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

case "$(uname -m)" in
x86_64) cpu=amd64 ;;
aarch64 | arm64) cpu=arm64 ;;
*) fail "Gate has no build for this server's CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

want="${GATE_VERSION:-latest}"
case "$want" in latest | v*) ;; *) want="v$want" ;; esac
if ! tag=$(gh-release tag minekube/gate "$want" 2>&1); then
    case "$tag" in
    *"has no release"*) fail "Gate has no release ${GATE_VERSION}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 0.81.1." ;;
    *) fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again." ;;
    esac
fi
asset="gate_${tag#v}_linux_$cpu"
assets=$(gh-release assets minekube/gate "$tag") || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
sum=$(awk -v a="$asset" '$1 == a { print $2; f = 1 } END { exit !f }' <<<"$assets") ||
    fail "Gate $tag has no Linux build for this CPU ($cpu). Choose another version."

if [ -x gate ] && [ "$sum" != - ] && [ "$(sha256sum gate | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "Gate $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Gate $tag"
    # gh-release puts the file in place only once it has arrived and checked out.
    gh-release download minekube/gate "$tag" "$asset" gate || fail "The download from GitHub failed or didn't match GitHub's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    chmod +x gate
fi

# Gate's own documented settings file, the first time: the full one, or its
# Lite (routes by hostname) or Bedrock cross-play example.
if [ ! -s config.yml ]; then
    type="${CONFIG_TYPE:-full}"
    ./gate config --type "$type" > config.yml.new || { rm -f config.yml.new; fail "Gate couldn't write its $type settings file."; }
    mv -f config.yml.new config.yml
    echo "Wrote Gate's $type settings to config.yml."
fi
echo "Installed Gate $tag for $cpu."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Gate release, such as 0.81.1, or latest for the newest one. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: Settings template
variables.description: The settings file Gate starts with the first time: full (every option, explained), simple (a short example), or lite (routes players to servers by hostname). An existing config.yml is never replaced.
